newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - Jan 7.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - Jan 7.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Indonesian stocks on Tuesday:
* President Suharto on Monday unveiled Indonesia's state budget for the coming fiscal year which aims to maintain the momentum of economic growth while curbing inflation and boosting exports.

* Suharto said 1996/97 economic growth was expected to be around the 8.2 percent figure of the previous year, while the budget will expand by 11.6 percent compared with 1996/97 to 101.09 trillion rupiah and the current account deficit was expected to be $8.823 billion in 1996/97, or 4.0 percent of GDP.
* Suharto said inflation was 6.47 percent in the 1996 calendar year, compared with 8.64 percent in 1995. Inflation was projected at six percent for 1997.
* The Dow Jones industrials rose 23.09 points to 6,567.18 on Monday, building on its 44 record finishes in 1996 amid a growing perception that the U.S. economy was still expanding at a solid pace.

* The Jakarta Composite Index rose 7.76 points, or 1.20 percent, to close at 653.96 points on Monday as more investors re-entered the market after the New Year holiday combined with positive news from the domestic economy.
* On Tuesday, the rupiah was quoted at 2,362.35/62.50 in early trading against the opening of 2,362.25/63.00.
* Astra Internasional following an announcement that the automobile conglomerate had launched new models of its popular Kijang van.
* Textile firm Mayertex following an announcement of a tender offer plan by privately-owned PT Ciptawira Binamandiri.
* Indosat on an announcement it planned to spend 490 billion rupiah in 1997 for expansion programme to boost net profit.
* Property firm Summarecon on market talk that the firm was likely to acquire another property firm and announce a rights issue.
